content.text:
The drawing shows a pyrimidine core with an anilino group at one carbon and a quinolin-6-yl group at another.

**Pyrimidine ring.** The ring atoms are C4 (bearing NH), C5 (CH), C6 (bearing the quinolinyl group), N1, C2 (CH) and N3. The two nitrogens are drawn at the bottom left and bottom right, with the CH between them. Reading around the ring, the NH-bearing carbon is bonded to N3, then C2, then N1, then C6 (bearing the quinolinyl group), then C5, and back to C4.

**Anilino group.** The NH links C4 to a benzene ring. That ring carries CF3 at the para position.

**Quinoline.** The quinoline is attached through its benzo ring, at the position para to the ring-fusion carbon that bonds to N. The drawing gives the fusion carbons as C8a (bonded to N1) at the upper left of the pyridine ring and C4a at the lower left. The attachment carbon is the one at the lower left of the benzo ring, next to C4a. Counting from C4a, the benzo carbons run C5, C6, C7, C8. C5 is adjacent to C4a, and the attachment carbon is next to that, so it is C6.

**SMILES.** Writing the pyrimidine as c1(Nc2ccc(C(F)(F)F)cc2)cc(-c2ccc3ncccc3c2)ncn1 gives the quinoline as c2ccc3ncccc3c2. In that string the attachment atom is c2, then c, c, and c3 (which is C8a, bonded to n). Going the other way from the attachment atom, the final c2 is C5 and the c3 before it is C4a. This makes the attachment atom C6, which matches the drawing.

SMILES: FC(F)(F)c1ccc(Nc2cc(-c3ccc4ncccc4c3)ncn2)cc1
